summary: Wireless Android Auto on the NBT Evo ID6 screen, with no extra hardware
author: nanaisu
description:
Android Auto on the car's own screen, run by the head unit itself. Your phone connects wirelessly, and Android Auto is an entry in the iDrive Media/Radio menu.

What works
- Wireless connection: Bluetooth first, then the car's Wi-Fi
- Touch, including two-finger pinch, and the iDrive controller and keys
- Media and navigation prompts over the phone's Bluetooth audio
- Google Assistant with the car's microphone
- The car's GPS position, speed, gear, night mode and driving status sent to the phone
- Android Auto steps aside for the reversing camera and comes back afterwards
- A Settings page in the menu: start automatically, save logs to USB, show iDrive warnings and more
- Optional: turn arrows in the instrument cluster and head-up display (Supra J29), and Android Auto over USB (beta)

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6)
- Apple CarPlay on the car: the phone joins the car's CarPlay Wi-Fi hotspot. A Settings option uses the car's Wi-Fi Direct network in its place
- Apps enabled in the car's coding: one of A4A, A4A_REMOTE_APPS, REMOTE_HMI or TOUCH_COMMAND
- An Android phone with wireless Android Auto, paired with the car over Bluetooth for calls

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open Media/Radio, choose Android Auto, then Start. The first connection often needs the phone to be paired with the car again as a new Bluetooth device.

Good to know
- If Android Auto was installed on this car by hand before, that install has to go first. With agent 1.4.0 or later the app finds it and shows what it would do: move the old plugin's folder aside into /opt/aa, where iDrive no longer loads it, and remove the rest. Nothing is changed until you confirm
- AAIdrive running at the same time can stop it from working
- Developed on the Toyota GR Supra (J29) and confirmed by users on a number of BMW models. Retrofits and bench setups are not supported by the author
